previous_statement: At each level put F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z_n(Y)-z_n(XY)+z_n(X)v_n(Y). Expanding g_n and using associativity of M_n tensor B gives v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z)=(v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)), whose norm is at most 2 epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| when d+epsilon<=1/4. In F_(w_prime), successively replace v_n(X)v_n(I tensor A_j) by v_n(X(I tensor A_j)); use X D=D X under the bilinear map (C,D)->v_n(C)g_n(D,Y); apply the displayed cocycle identity to (I tensor B_j,X,Y); reassociate v_n(I tensor A_j)(v_n(I tensor B_j)g_n(X,Y)); replace the first two factors by v_n(I tensor A_j B_j); sum using pi(D)=I; and replace v_n(I)g_n(X,Y) by g_n(X,Y). The d-multiplicativity, epsilon-associativity, approximate-unit, and product bounds control these seven replacements respectively by fixed multiples of d^2, epsilon*d, epsilon, epsilon*d, d^2, zero, and (d+epsilon)d, each weighted by sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1. Thus their sum is at most 100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||, uniformly in n.
new_statement: Fix n and suppose D=sum_j A_j tensor B_j is a diagonal with sum_j||A_j||||B_j||=1. Put a_j=I_n tensor A_j, b_j=I_n tensor B_j, g_n(X,Y)=v_n(XY)-v_n(X)v_n(Y), w_prime_(D,n)(X)=sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,X), and F_z(X,Y)=v_n(X)z(Y)-z(XY)+z(X)v_n(Y). These are local hypotheses and definitions; no existence of D and no identification w_prime_(D,n)=I_n tensor w_prime is asserted here. Direct expansion gives v_n(X)g_n(Y,Z)-g_n(XY,Z)+g_n(X,YZ)-g_n(X,Y)v_n(Z)=(v_n(X)v_n(Y))v_n(Z)-v_n(X)(v_n(Y)v_n(Z)); since ||v_n(T)||<=(1+d)||T||, the epsilon-associativity bound makes the residual at most epsilon(1+d)^3||X||||Y||||Z||<=2epsilon||X||||Y||||Z|| when d+epsilon<=1/4. Expand F_(w_prime_(D,n)). First reassociate v_n(X)(v_n(a_j)g_n(b_j,Y)) and replace v_n(X)v_n(a_j) by v_n(Xa_j). Entrywise amplification of XD=DX then changes sum_j v_n(Xa_j)g_n(b_j,Y) exactly into sum_j v_n(a_j)g_n(b_jX,Y). Reassociate the third term to put v_n(a_j) outside, and apply the displayed cocycle identity to (b_j,X,Y), obtaining sum_j v_n(a_j)(v_n(b_j)g_n(X,Y)) up to its residual. Reassociate this expression, replace v_n(a_j)v_n(b_j) by v_n(a_jb_j), and use sum_j a_jb_j=I_n tensor pi(D)=I. Finally replace v_n(I)g_n(X,Y) by g_n(X,Y). After summing in j, the respective errors are bounded by epsilon(1+d)^2 d, (1+epsilon)d^2, epsilon(1+d)^2 d, 2(1+epsilon)(1+d)epsilon, epsilon(1+d)^2 d, (1+epsilon)d^2, and ((1+epsilon)d+epsilon)d, all multiplied by ||X||||Y|| sum_j||A_j||||B_j||. For d+epsilon<=1/4 their sum is at most 100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Hence ||F_(w_prime_(D,n))(X,Y)-g_n(X,Y)||<=100(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y|| uniformly in n and in every normalized diagonal satisfying the stated local hypothesis.
